original_card.first_experiment: Choose one latest uncovered candidate and build a delta coverage map against the selected review. For P104, #5717 changes owned-lifetime assumptions and #5719 covers exact #5713 causal premises; neither automatically transfers to #5718. original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.

actual_scope: Exact set of kappa for which the selected #5599 outer ledger (PR4359 54 strict checks plus 4 functional checks, as called by research/p104-helper-subspace-splits/pricing.py) is satisfiable, as a function of the complex uniform saving U and admitted BIT saving B.
scope_change_reason: Original target chosen at the open-question checkpoint. Instead of auditing one changed supplier, this settles the outer-admission step that every changed supplier must pass: it gives the exact supplier conditions the selected outer ledger imposes, which revision 8 asks contributors aiming at kappa > .01 to work out.
bottleneck_link: Revision 8 says to work backward from the nine outer rows for kappa > .01. This proves those rows require exactly U > kappa and B > kappa (and kappa < 1/32), so supplier savings, not the outer ledger, are the binding constraint.
stop_rule: Stop after the written proof, exact corroboration and one focused PR.

open_questions.question: Does any proposed joint complex/BIT supplier trade improve kappa under this ledger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The admissible region depends only on min(U, B), so a trade helps only while U < B.
open_questions.first_step: State the trade as (delta U, delta B) and apply the min.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such joint supplier exists yet.
